scope: Mandatory encrypted checkpoints for combined report submission and all seven later circuits
behavior: An active combined autosave writer is required before network report actions. Guided-local actions remain local.
An exclusive persistence lease cancels pending debounce and suppresses new draft writes during the transaction; existing writes stay serialized.
Before SDK/private-state work, a v8 snapshot saves report recovery material, uncertainty and immutable requested circuit/report/state/severity/private notes.
Before wallet broadcast, the same revision-checked copy must confirm the canonical 64- or 66-character transaction identifier.

SDK confirmation must match circuit and identifier. The final result is saved before releasing persistence. A final save failure preserves matching SDK confirmation in memory, stops autosave and requests a file backup.
Preparation/checkpoint wait is 15 minutes, post-checkpoint confirmation 10 minutes, final result save 1 minute. Late checkpoints cannot authorize broadcast after closure.
V8 validates journal shape, immutable inputs, unique identifiers and pending/uncertain bindings. Private recovery exposes historical requests and explicit read-only lookup.

developmentFailures.cause: Existing integration assertions did not wait for new encrypted saves; one overall test deadline was also too short.
Overall restored-report test deadline and interaction with still-disabled controls needed to await durable saves.
One remaining audit assertion still used the old non-hex patch transaction fixture.
New journal-view assertion contained a question mark introduced by shell encoding instead of the rendered middle dot.

limitations: Wallet and SDK calls are mocked in application network tests. No native signing/broadcast, authenticated inclusion or proof verification is claimed.

Unknown report attempts remain blocked after restore. A pending report already present on the ledger still cannot be promoted automatically; safe retry and full effect/argument reconciliation remain open.
SDK/provider work and already-started storage operations may continue after deadlines. Physical crash/suspend behavior was not tested.
Report preparation/ciphertext upload can precede the initial transaction checkpoint.
At most 1000 entries are retained. Old report metadata does not replace separate backups of their report decryption material. V1-v7 stay readable; older application releases cannot read v8.
No full repository regression, container runtime refresh or security scan is claimed in this increment.
